children: The Bank of England's decision to reduce the pace of quantitative tighening could have an insignificant effect on the gilt market, RBC BlueBay Asset Management's Neil Mehta says in a note. The BOE announced a slower pace of quantitative tightening to an average of 46 billion pounds annually, from 70 billion pounds per year currently. Although the announcement has caused gilt yields to edge lower, the government bonds still face pressure from inflation concerns and fiscal jitters, Mehta says. Ten-year gilt yields drop to last trade at 5.213%, from 5.295% prior to the announcement, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
